candidates.title: Guest console output re-enters mcycle hash collection on every character when console output is to_buffer, multiplying collection cost per mcycle by about 100x or more and writing a stderr line per character
candidates.role: Honest operator: collect_mcycle_root_hashes is listed in the AUDIT.md component table. collect_mcycle_bundle is part of the rest of the machine API, honest operator where a production node calls it. The to_buffer console runtime option is only on the honest operator's path if a production node configures it, which this hunt cannot confirm, so both ratings are given.
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp interpret_with_console (around line 2253: returns console_output to the caller when the destination is to_buffer); collect_mcycle_root_hashes (around 2426-2600: every call runs update_hash_tree(), which re-marks and rehashes the always-dirty shadow-register, shadow-TLB and uarch-state pages (machine-address-ranges.cpp:129), then reserve(16384) hashes and 4096 dirty pages, and the loop ends on any break reason other than reached_target_mcycle); collect_mcycle_bundle (around 2603-2670: loops over collect_mcycle_root_hashes and never drains the buffer); src/machine-console.cpp putchars (line 55: should_flush = available_output_buffer_space()==0 or newline/every_char) and append_output (line 412: when full, it fprintf(stderr, WARNING...) and drops the oldest byte, so the buffer stays full and each later putchar breaks again).
candidates.description: When the console output destination is to_buffer, putchar returns should_flush on every newline (every_line, the default flush mode), on every character (every_char), or, once the 4096-byte buffer is full, on every character in any mode. This holds because append_output makes room by discarding the oldest byte, so the buffer stays full. Each such putchar ends the interpreter loop with success_and_console_output. interpret_with_console then returns console_output to its caller, because with to_buffer the caller must drain the buffer. In collect_mcycle_root_hashes, that break ends the call. The caller must call again, and each new call pays a fixed entry cost, about 30 microseconds as measured. That cost comes from update_hash_tree() rehashing the always-dirty pages (shadow registers, the whole shadow TLB, the uarch state), the 512 KiB reserve of the result vector, and the dirty-page reserve. collect_mcycle_bundle loops internally and cannot let its caller drain the buffer, so after 4096 characters every guest putchar becomes one such re-entry. Each one also writes an 86-byte WARNING line to the host's stderr. The state hashes stay correct: the measured hashes are identical across console configurations, so R14's 'must not affect the state' holds. The cost of an R12 operation, however, depends on guest output and a host runtime option. The extra cost does not come from the specified semantics: the manual's putchar only outputs a character, while the re-entry and the rehash of the always-dirty pages are implementation overhead.
candidates.trigger: Any guest, including one fully controlled by an input (THREAT_MODEL section 4: the guest is adversarial for containment), emits console characters through HTIF putchar, which is enabled by default (iconsole = putchar) in reproducible machines. A store to tohost suffices, so one character can cost one mcycle. Precondition on the host: the honest operator's machine runs with console output_destination = to_buffer, a documented runtime option (cm runtime config, Lua {console={output_destination='to_buffer'}}).
candidates.reachability: Reachable from every valid template: HTIF putchar is enabled by default and any guest-writable instruction stream can write tohost. Measured on audit/prt2 with a bare-metal guest that loops on cm_putchar('\n') 200000 times (1.0M mcycles).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The trigger is guest console output plus a documented host runtime option, not a deliberate state change, an untrusted API caller, an unguaranteed directory, or a host fault. Section 8 excludes 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields', but console characters are neither outputs nor yields, and the exclusion holds only 'as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)'. Not out of scope, unless triage reads the console as covered by that exclusion. 2 Role: collect_mcycle_root_hashes is in the AUDIT.md table as honest operator. collect_mcycle_bundle is honest operator if a production node calls it. The PRT player in doc/recipes (support) uses the default to_stdout console, where the effect is only about 3x (one write syscall per newline). 3 High/Medium cases: section 8 High: 'A defect that lets the guest, or host load that the deployment was sized for, multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect, while staying within what the deployment was sized for. A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect. When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High and a super-linear or unbounded one Critical.' R12: 'Each of the following operations has a worst case in host time and memory that is bounded and at most linear in the cycles it executes ... a part of a claim'. The cost stays linear but grows by a constant factor of about 117x (collect_mcycle_bundle, when_full, buffer not drained: 6.07 s against 0.052 s with to_null) or about 200x (collect_mcycle_root_hashes, every_char, drained each break: 6.39 s against 0.032 s). This matches the High case. 4 Critical: it would be Critical only if the factor pushes the cost past what the deployment was sized for (the 'larger than what the deployment was sized for' entry). That depends on the released COMMITMENT_BUDGET sizing and on whether a production node uses to_buffer. 5 Low: if no production node uses to_buffer, only the support PRT player is affected, and it uses to_stdout. That is a support defect rated Medium at most (section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'), or Low. Deciding facts: whether production validator nodes configure console output to_buffer, and the sizing in docs/measurements/constants.md of Dave.
candidates.claimed_severity: High (honest operator with a to_buffer console, sizing unknown); Medium/Low if to_buffer is used only by support tools
candidates.threat_to_goal: A7/R12: the dispute clocks (COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 minutes for every inner commitment in the released ArbitrationConstants.sol) are sized from the honest operator's bulk leaf-path cost. An adversarial input can make the guest print a character per mcycle, which multiplies the honest operator's mcycle-level collection cost by two to three orders of magnitude. Past the sizing margin, the honest claim times out. That is a completeness failure, after which a dishonest claim can win. The stderr line per character also grows host logs by 86 bytes per guest mcycle.
candidates.evidence: Scratch /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R14/: src/nl.c (loop of 200000 cm_putchar('\n'), then halt), built with bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh into nl.bin and nop.bin; bench.lua and bench2.lua. Results (1,000,026 mcycles, identical final root hash 0x0f20b421... in every case): run with to_null 0.014 s; run with to_stdout every_line (file) 0.083 s; run with to_buffer every_char (drained) 0.166 s, 200000 breaks; collect_mcycle_root_hashes(MCYCLE_MAX, 20, ...) looped: to_null 0.032 s, to_stdout 0.094 s, to_buffer every_char (drained each break) 6.391 s; collect_mcycle_bundle(0, 10, 10): to_null 0.052 s, to_buffer when_full (not drained) 6.065 s with 391,808 'WARNING: console output buffer is out of space' lines on stderr, to_buffer every_line 6.591 s.
candidates.test_idea: Load nl.bin (or a bare-metal guest built in bugs/<ID>/) twice: once with console to_null and once with {output_destination='to_buffer', output_flush_mode='when_full'}. Run collect_mcycle_bundle(0, 10, 10) in a child process with stderr captured. Assert deterministically that the to_buffer run writes no stderr warning (it currently writes about 390k lines) and that the bundles are equal. Optionally also assert a generous cost bound: time(to_buffer) < 5 x time(to_null) (it is currently over 100x).

candidates.title: Manual does not state the host requirement that console output channels accept every write, blocking if needed, which THREAT_MODEL section 4 says it must
candidates.component: doc/README.md (manual) for the console runtime configuration; behavior in src/machine-console.cpp flush_output and src/os.cpp putchars/write_fd
candidates.role: Honest operator (the documentation of the host setup that the honest operator's emulator relies on). The manual is the specification.
candidates.location: doc/README.md: no section documents console runtime options (output_destination, output_flush_mode, to_fd/to_file) or what the host output channel must provide. grep for 'accept every', 'non-blocking', 'EAGAIN' and 'runtime config' finds nothing. Code: machine_console::flush_output (src/machine-console.cpp:254-310) does one write(2). EPIPE is silently discarded, any other error (for example EAGAIN on a non-blocking stdout or pipe) throws machine_console_exception out of machine::run, and a partial write keeps the rest buffered.
candidates.description: THREAT_MODEL section 4 says: 'Host output channels, such as the console, accept every write the emulator makes, blocking if needed, and the manual must state this requirement.' The manual of audit/prt2 never states it. The emulator relies on it: with a non-blocking or failing descriptor, flush_output throws machine_console_exception from machine::run. collect_mcycle_root_hashes catches the exception, clears the output and continues, recording console_io_error. collect_mcycle_bundle swallows it. An operator who wires the console to a non-blocking pipe (a common supervisor or logging setup), or whose stdout is closed, gets run() failures or silently lost logs. Nothing in the manual tells the operator this is a misconfiguration. No wrong hash results: the state is committed before the throw, and the measured hashes are unaffected.
candidates.trigger: Host configuration: console output to a non-blocking file descriptor (EAGAIN) or a descriptor that errors. The guest only needs to print.
candidates.reachability: Any guest that prints, from any valid template, with such a host setup.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? A host fault 'may stop the honest operator', which is excluded 'as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash...'. That exclusion covers the run failure itself, but not the missing manual statement, which section 4 makes a requirement of the manual. 2 Role: the manual as the specification of the honest operator's host setup. 3 Medium cases: no listed case fits exactly. The closest is 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' This is an omission, not a contradiction. 4 Critical: no rule of section 6 is violated at a reachable state, and the operator's path stops only on a host fault, which the model permits. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'. Section 4's 'must state' is, however, an explicit requirement of the model, which may lift it to Medium ('violates a rule or the manual without affecting the goal'). Claimed: Low, possibly Medium, depending on whether triage treats section 4's 'must state' as a rule.
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the goal directly. An honest operator on an undocumented host setup (non-blocking log pipe) can see machine::run throw while advancing its machine, which may stop or delay its defense (R4: 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'), with no documented reason.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of machine-console.cpp flush_output, os.cpp putchars/write_fd and machine.cpp interpret_with_console/collect_*; grep of doc/README.md. Not run.
candidates.test_idea: A documentation check: assert that doc/README.md contains a statement of the console output requirement. Behavioral: set the console runtime config to_fd with a non-blocking pipe whose reader never reads, run the putchar guest, and assert that run() either blocks until the pipe is drained or that the documented behavior holds.

not_covered: VirtIO device implementations themselves (virtio-*-address-range.cpp): rejected at creation for reproducible machines (push_back_virtio), so only that guard was checked

Interrupt deferral between native inner loop and uarch per-mcycle interrupt checks (assert_no_brk allows pending M-mode interrupts in S/U mode): only reasoned briefly (CLINT/PLIC/CSR writes return success_and_serve_interrupts); left to the R2 hunter
Fetch-cache vs shadow-TLB equivalence across console/soft-yield breaks (resume re-translates through the TLB): reasoned only, no differential test
Uarch-level equivalence of HTIF putchar (uarch ECALL putchar and solidity putCharECALL no-op): code read only, no EVM run
Concurrency runtime option (update_hash_tree threads), clear_hash_tree and no_reserve: left to R1/R9 hunters
JSON-RPC server console/runtime defaults and fork/clone of unreproducible machines: only grep-level
Whether production validator nodes (out of scope) use to_buffer consoles: unknown, decides the severity of candidate 1
machine-guest-tools console usage (guest-side printing frequency limits): not examined

write_reg/set_runtime_config ability to change iunrep/iconsole on a live reproducible machine: noted as deliberate machine-API changes (out of scope); iunrep is read by the emulator from the config (m_c), not from the hashed shadow register, which only matters after write_reg(iunrep)
